title: The reader at the counter
logline: Monday. A stranger at Gully's reads the strip in the weekly and laughs. Not a tourist; a local. The first local reader the strip has seen since the laundromat. Wood draws the laugh and not the man.

panels.composition: Gully's. A LOCAL in a rain hood at the counter with the weekly. WOOD on the end stool, three seats down. GULLY. BARNABY.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a local in a rain hood reading a newspaper at a bait-shop counter three stools from a thin man, a man in an apron, a dog

panels.composition: The laugh. Drawn as a small shape over the hood. The paper shaking.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, close-up of a newspaper shaking in a reader's hands with a small laugh shape above a rain hood

panels.composition: Wood not looking. Looking. The pad: the laugh shape, alone, no face.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man drawing a small laugh shape on a pad without drawing the person who laughed

panels.composition: The local folding the paper. Leaving it on the counter for the next one. Gully sliding it down to Wood. Wood sliding it back up.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a newspaper being slid along a counter from a man in an apron to a thin man who slides it back, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: A local laughs. The laugh drawn, not the man. The paper slid back.
